pr.title: coverage: Don't store a body span in `FunctionCoverageInfo`
pr.description: We aren't using this body span for anything truly essential, and having it around will be awkward when we eventually start to support expansion regions, since they aren't necessarily within the main body.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: Coverage instrumentation no longer stores a function body span in `FunctionCoverageInfo`. Empty coverage spans are still enlarged to an adjacent `{`/`}` by one ASCII byte, but the expansion is now bounded by source-file access instead of the function body span. File selection for region tables now uses the first coverage mapping's span rather than the body span.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, `FunctionCoverageInfo` carried `body_span`, assigned as `body_span: hir_info.body_span`. `ensure_non_empty_span` used that span as the boundary for expanding empty coverage spans: `let try_next = hi < fn_cov_info.body_span.hi();` and `let try_prev = fn_cov_info.body_span.lo() < lo;` followed by `if !(try_next || try_prev) { return None; }`. Region/source-file lookup also used the body span: `let source_file = source_map.lookup_source_file(fn_cov_info.body_span.lo());`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation gated adjacent-brace expansion of empty coverage spans on the stored function body span, so an empty span at the body boundary could not expand outward even if the neighboring source character was `{` or `}`. The patch removes that dependency, replacing the body-span bounds with source-file bounds: `if src.as_bytes().get(end).copied() == Some(b'{') {` and `} else if start > 0 && src.as_bytes()[start - 1] == b'}' {`. A rewrite that merely deletes `body_span` storage while keeping the old body-span-based expansion conditions would not compile correctly/faithfully; the correct removal also changes the expansion boundary and file lookup anchor.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented Rust functions whose `FunctionCoverageInfo` contains at least one `Mapping` with an empty source span, especially empty spans located exactly at the start or end of the function body and adjacent to an opening or closing brace. Also covers functions whose mappings must all belong to one source file, now located via the first mapping rather than the body span.
analysis.trigger: An empty coverage mapping span is encountered at the function-body boundary, adjacent to `{` or `}`, and the old code's `try_next`/`try_prev` body-span checks would have rejected expansion.
preconditions: The function has `FunctionCoverageInfo` with at least one mapping; region-table generation now asserts `function has no mappings` otherwise
The empty span is adjacent to an ASCII `{` or `}` in the source file
The neighboring byte is within the source-file text, with `start > 0` required for backward expansion
All mappings for the function are expected to be in the same source file, anchored by the first mapping's span
pitfalls: The test line-number changes in `instrument_coverage.main.InstrumentCoverage.diff` (for example `14:1: 14:11` becoming `13:1: 13:11`) are caused by deleting CHECK lines from the test source, not by changed coverage mapping semantics.
Removing the `coverage body span:` debug line is not itself evidence that mapping expansion behavior changed; inspect `ensure_non_empty_span` separately.
The `BytePos(1)` adjustment is only valid because the skipped character has been checked to be one of two specific ASCII braces.

Forward expansion previously relied on slicing bounds; the new code uses `src.as_bytes().get(end)` to avoid an out-of-bounds access, while backward expansion still needs an explicit `start > 0` guard.
Do not attribute this behavior to `CleanupPostBorrowck`; that pass's diff only loses the printed body-span line.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the `tests/mir-opt/coverage` mir-opt tests with coverage instrumentation and `EMIT_MIR` for the `InstrumentCoverage` pass. In `tests/mir-opt/coverage/instrument_coverage.rs`, remove or assert absence of `coverage body span:` and keep checks for `coverage Code { bcb: bcbN } =>`. Construct paired functions that differ only by an empty coverage span at the body boundary next to `{`/`}`: one where the old body-span bound would suppress expansion and one where the brace is interior. Compare emitted `InstrumentCoverage` mappings for retained versus dropped spans. Also verify that file selection uses the first mapping span and that functions with no mappings hit only the debug assertion path rather than source-map lookup.
